source.spec_title: EL-GS v8.3 — Formal Specification (gate document, revision 4)
source.auxiliary_citation_policy: Sections 1 and 5 are the normative source. Text outside 1 and 5 is cited only where sections 1/5 explicitly delegate (evidence ownership, ledger constants, gauge re-anchoring, per-case delta-psi) and is always tagged with its own section label.
source.quote_policy: Every field named "quote", "quote_N", "*_quote" or "verbatim" is a verbatim substring of the source file after whitespace normalization (source line wraps joined with a single space after stripping leading indentation); no other edit. Fields named "rule", "formula", "text" or "note" may paraphrase and are anchored by a neighbouring quote.
source.transcription_note: This file is an independent transcription intended as a unit-test oracle. Cells the spec does not fix are marked with "spec_silent": true and a note; no semantics were invented.
source.precedence_note: §1 is the canonical interval-state definition and overrides every earlier dimension or encoding statement in the same file; earlier-revision sentences survive only as history.
source.precedence_quote: This section is the single source of truth for the interval state; it consolidates the rev-2/rev-3 latch-bit and simplex fragments and supersedes every earlier dimension or encoding statement.
source.supersession_tag_quote: Superseded sentences below are tagged [SUPERSEDED → §1] / [SUPERSEDED → §7] and are retained only as revision history.
source.supersession_tag_note: Any sentence carrying a [SUPERSEDED → §1] / [SUPERSEDED → §7] tag was NOT transcribed as normative; nothing in this table is sourced from a tagged sentence.

state_tuple.notation: l_pre = ℓ_pre, l_post = ℓ_post (ASCII aliases used in JSON keys only; the spec writes ℓ)
state_tuple.quote: Persist per family: (K_f, ℓ_pre, ℓ_post, a) in the canonical coordinate order

episode_cap.quote: Families f ∈ F with presence program P_f of K_f ≤ 4 episodes.

admissible_latch_patterns.semantics: ℓ_pre = 1 ⇔ b_1 = −w_m exactly; ℓ_post = 1 ⇔ d_{K_f} = T + w_m exactly
admissible_latch_patterns.toggling: toggled ONLY by structural ops (§5), never by gradient steps; carry no optimizer state
admissible_latch_patterns.quote: All four patterns (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), (1,1) are admissible; a latch anywhere else (interior endpoints) is inadmissible.
admissible_latch_patterns.quote_2: Latch bits are toggled ONLY by structural ops (§5), never by gradient steps, and carry no optimizer state.
admissible_latch_patterns.domain: K_f ≥ 1 (a K_f = 0 family carries no latch bits at all)
admissible_latch_patterns.quote_3: Each family with K_f ≥ 1 carries exactly two latch bits (ℓ_pre, ℓ_post) ∈ {0,1}²

dimension_formula.composition: (2 − n_lat) unlatched outer slacks + K_f lengths + (K_f−1) gaps
dimension_formula.loader_check: the loader MUST validate dim(a) = 2K_f + 1 − n_lat (K_f = 0 persists as the empty program with no latch bits)
dimension_formula.quote: n_lat := ℓ_pre + ℓ_post. Raw vector a ∈ R^{2K_f+1−n_lat}, i.e. (2 − n_lat) unlatched outer slacks + K_f lengths + (K_f−1) gaps.
dimension_formula.loader_check_quote: the loader MUST validate dim(a) = 2K_f + 1 − n_lat (K_f = 0 persists as the empty program with no latch bits)

canonical_coordinate_order.rule: [slack_pre iff ℓ_pre=0], len_1, gap_1, …, gap_{K_f−1}, len_{K_f}, [slack_post iff ℓ_post=0]
canonical_coordinate_order.quote: Canonical coordinate order (also the serialization order): [slack_pre iff ℓ_pre=0], len_1, gap_1, …, gap_{K_f−1}, len_{K_f}, [slack_post iff ℓ_post=0].

omega.admissibility: an op is admissible only if Ω_free > 0
omega.latch_independence: Ω_free NEVER depends on the latch pattern — a latched slack is identically zero and simply has no coordinate
omega.quote: Ω = T + 2w_m; Ω_free = Ω − K_f·floor_len − (K_f−1)·floor_gap (an op is admissible only if Ω_free > 0; Ω_free NEVER depends on the latch pattern — a latched slack is identically zero and simply has no coordinate).

forward_map.left_endpoint: b_1 = −w_m + slack_pre; endpoints follow by summation
forward_map.budget_identity: slack_pre + Σ_k len_k + Σ_k gap_k + slack_post = Ω for every latch pattern
forward_map.right_endpoint_bound: d_{K_f} ≤ T + w_m holds IDENTICALLY under any optimizer step, with equality iff ℓ_post = 1
forward_map.quote: σ = softmax(a); each unlatched slack = Ω_free·σ_(its coord); each latched slack ≡ 0; len_k = floor_len + Ω_free·σ_(len_k); gap_k = floor_gap + Ω_free·σ_(gap_k).
forward_map.quote_2: d_{K_f} ≤ T + w_m holds IDENTICALLY under any optimizer step, with equality iff ℓ_post = 1.

inverse_map.used_by: every structural op, to write the child state
inverse_map.target_admissibility: admissible target = (latch pattern; every unlatched slack > 0 strictly; every len_k > floor_len and gap_k > floor_gap strictly)
inverse_map.logits: a_i = log σ_i − max_j log σ_j
inverse_map.gauge: gauge fixed so max a_i = 0; deterministic
inverse_map.floor_targets_inadmissible: An op whose target would put an unlatched coordinate exactly at its floor is inadmissible as stated
inverse_map.zero_outer_slack_target: a target with an outer slack exactly 0 must set the corresponding latch instead
inverse_map.quote: Given an admissible target (latch pattern; every unlatched slack > 0 strictly; every len_k > floor_len and gap_k > floor_gap strictly): σ_i = (value_i − floor_i)/Ω_free (floor_i = 0 for slacks), then a_i = log σ_i − max_j log σ_j (gauge fixed so max a_i = 0; deterministic).
inverse_map.quote_2: An op whose target would put an unlatched coordinate exactly at its floor is inadmissible as stated; a target with an outer slack exactly 0 must set the corresponding latch instead.

exact_boundary_rule.rule: Exact boundary contact is representable ONLY by a latch bit; a zero slack coordinate does not exist and no op may target one.
exact_boundary_rule.quote: Softmax coordinates are strictly positive, so every unlatched slack is strictly > 0: exact boundary contact is representable ONLY by a latch bit.
exact_boundary_rule.quote_2: A "zero slack coordinate" does not exist in this parameterization and no op may target one.

k_zero_convention.rule: K_f = 0 is a defined state (empty program): no latch bits, no vector a; renders nothing; prune-pending.
k_zero_convention.quote: K_f = 0: defined state (empty program) — no latch bits, no vector a; renders nothing; prune-pending (unchanged from v8.2).
k_zero_convention.serialization: K_f = 0 persists as the empty program with no latch bits

rules: an op that preserves an outer endpoint preserves its latch
an op that deletes the outermost episode on a side DISCARDS that side's latch (the new outer slack enters as an unlatched coordinate via the inverse map)
TRUNCATE-shorten applied to a latched outer endpoint CLEARS that latch
REACTIVATE insertion outside a latched outer endpoint is inadmissible (zero room)
MERGE: ℓ_pre is taken from the parent owning the globally earliest b_1, ℓ_post from the parent owning the globally latest d_K
interior ops (interior fission/truncation/reactivation/prune) never touch latches
latch_inheritance_summary.quote: An op that preserves an outer endpoint preserves its latch; an op that deletes the outermost episode on a side DISCARDS that side's latch (the new outer slack enters as an unlatched coordinate via the inverse map); TRUNCATE-shorten applied to a latched outer endpoint CLEARS that latch; REACTIVATE insertion outside a latched outer endpoint is inadmissible (zero room); MERGE: ℓ_pre is taken from the parent owning the globally earliest b_1, ℓ_post from the parent owning the globally latest d_K; BIRTH sets (ℓ_pre, ℓ_post) = (0,1) (§5); interior ops (interior fission/truncation/reactivation/prune) never touch latches.
latch_inheritance_summary.quote_2: children of terminal ops inherit the parent's outer latch on the surviving side; interior ops never touch latches

all_ops_rule.rule: Every op writes its child interval state through the §1 inverse map; §1 alone governs latch inheritance, exact-boundary handling, target admissibility, and moment resets.
all_ops_rule.quote: every op writes its child interval state through the §1 inverse map (child dimension 2K′+1−n_lat′ per the child latch pattern); latch inheritance, exact-boundary handling, target admissibility, and moment resets are governed by §1 alone — no op table entry may encode a boundary as a zero coordinate.

optimizer_moments.rule: Every structural op rewrites a through the inverse map, so the family's simplex-logit moment state is RESET and the reset logged; latch bits never carry moments.
optimizer_moments.quote: Every structural op rewrites a through the inverse map (dimension and/or values change), so the family's simplex-logit moment state is RESET and the reset logged (rev-3 A1 unchanged). Latch bits never carry moments.

floors_and_symbols.plateau_indicator: z_f(t) = 1 iff t in a plateau [b_k+w, d_k−w]
floors_and_symbols.edge_bands: X_f = {t : |t − nearest edge| < w in frame units, strict}
floors_and_symbols.len_at_floor_predicate: "Len at floor" predicates are replaced by len ≤ floor + δ_tol (preregistered tolerance)

numeric_values.note: T, w, w_m, δ_len, δ_gap, δ_tol, r_site, κ, χ, μ, β, τ_B are symbolic/preregistered; no numeric values appear in §1 or §5.

ledger_constants.kappa: κ is charged PER EPISODE via κ·K_f (state term: refunded automatically when episodes are deleted)
ledger_constants.chi_mu: χ and μ are ledgered and never refunded; C(H) = χ·N_returnbirth(H) + μ·N_merge(H)
ledger_constants.quote: κ is charged PER EPISODE via κ·K_f (state term: refunded automatically when episodes are deleted); χ and μ are ledgered and never refunded.
ledger_constants.quote_section: §4 (cited because §5 uses κ, χ, μ without redefining them)

global_notes: K-change target allocation: the file states that K-change inverse maps come from "allocating the affected spans and re-normalizing the remaining simplex (deterministic formulas in the op table)" (header v8.2 item (1)), but the referenced deterministic per-op target formulas are NOT present in this document except for BIRTH, FISSION, and MERGE (operations[11] does state its child targets: the concatenated ordered episode intervals of both parents). For every other K-changing op the target VALUES handed to the §1 inverse map (i.e. where the freed or borrowed span goes) are spec_silent; the only binding constraint transcribed here is the §1 budget identity slack_pre + Σ len_k + Σ gap_k + slack_post = Ω.
Clone/split is not a §5 structural op: header v8.2 item (2) states it does not alter bind, and PROP 2 (§4) treats it as a family-membership change only. It therefore has no entry in this table.

DERIVED (arithmetic consequence of Ω_free = Ω − K·floor_len − (K−1)·floor_gap, not a spec sentence): ops that change K also change Ω_free, so all surviving coordinates are re-derived through the §1 inverse map even when their interval values are unchanged.
"derived": true marks arithmetic consequences of transcribed formulas, included for oracle convenience; they are not additional spec statements.

path_dependence.rule: Structural-op outcomes are path dependent; predicates are re-tested every round and there is no undo.
path_dependence.quote: Path-dependence disclosed; re-tested each round; no undo.

field_dictionary.case: short slug for one latch-distinguishable case of that op.
field_dictionary.k_change: integer ΔK_f of the single family whose interval state is rewritten; null when no single-family ΔK is defined — BIRTH (family creation, see child_K), MERGE (two families fuse, see k_change_note), PRUNE-family (family removal), and inadmissible candidates (no transition).
field_dictionary.child_K: absolute K of the child where it is a fixed number; when the child K is symbolic (MERGE: K_old + K_new) it is given in k_change_note instead.
field_dictionary.latch_effect.pattern_map: parent (ℓ_pre,ℓ_post) → child (ℓ_pre,ℓ_post); keyed by which side the op touches when the transition is side-dependent; valid only over the sibling "domain".
field_dictionary.domain: the K_f range over which the neighbouring rule / pattern_map / dimension formula holds; where a K_f = 1 boundary exists, see k_equals_one_row.
field_dictionary.k_equals_one_row: the K_f = 1 boundary row: the child is the §1 K=0 empty program (no latch bits, dim(a) = 0).
field_dictionary.spec_silent: true ⇒ the spec does not fix this cell; the sibling note states what is missing. A test oracle must not fill these in.
field_dictionary.derived: true ⇒ arithmetic or logical consequence of transcribed statements, supplied for oracle convenience; NOT a spec sentence.

operations.case_description: Creation of a new family f′ with a single episode and a latched terminal endpoint.
preconditions: len_1 > floor_len strictly
t_birth > −w_m, i.e. slack_pre > 0
§1 admissibility governs (in particular Ω_free > 0; at K=1, Ω_free = Ω − floor_len)
Admissible under caps; cap-saturated ⇒ INADMISSIBLE this round, re-eligible next (logged)
operations.k_change_note: No parent family exists, so ΔK is undefined (k_change = null); the child is created at K = 1 (child_K).

latch_effect.rule: BIRTH sets (ℓ_pre, ℓ_post) = (0,1): terminal latch, d_1 = T + w_m EXACT, represented by the latch bit, NOT by a zero slack coordinate (supersedes "slack_post = 0 at init").

derived_consistency_check.statement: slack_pre + len_1 = T + 2w_m = Ω, and σ_slack_pre + σ_len_1 = (slack_pre + len_1 − floor_len)/Ω_free = 1, so the §1 inverse map is well posed on the stated targets.

parameter_init.interval: targets slack_pre = t_birth + w_m, len_1 = T + w_m − t_birth (§5 BIRTH)

pose_motion_appearance.note: §5 BIRTH specifies only the interval targets and the latch; no pose, motion-coefficient, origin, or radiance initialization is stated in §1/§5.
pose_motion_appearance.delegation_quote: Rendering, pose/motion, gauge, pruning, caps: as [[operations/elgs-method]].
pose_motion_appearance.delegation_note: The silence is a DELEGATION to the prose method page, not freedom: §1 routes rendering, pose/motion, gauge, pruning and caps out of the formal spec. A test oracle must not invent an initializer here.

evidence_ownership.detail: clusters are ASSIGNED at binding by the single-valued map bind(u); U(f) := bind⁻¹(f); ℓ_b(P_f) sums ONLY over u ∈ U(f) (header v8.2 item (2))
evidence_ownership.note: No cluster binding is created by the BIRTH op itself.

delta_state.verbatim: Δ = +κ + ψ + LEDGER χ if at a return site.

expansion.text: ψ = ψ_dur(len_1); no ψ_gap term exists at K=1 because §4 sums Σ_{k<K_f} ψ_gap.

delta_ledger.chi: +χ if at a return site (increments N_returnbirth(H))

moment_reset.what_resets: the family's simplex-logit moment state (vacuous for a newly created family); latch bits never carry moments
moment_reset.note: §1 OPTIMIZER MOMENTS general rule; the §5 BIRTH entry does not restate it.

spec_quotes.quote: BIRTH(f′): K=1 with (ℓ_pre, ℓ_post) = (0, 1) — terminal latch: d_1 = T + w_m EXACT, represented by the latch bit, NOT by a zero slack coordinate (supersedes "slack_post = 0 at init").

State a ∈ R^2 = (slack_pre, len_1) via the §1 inverse map with targets slack_pre = t_birth + w_m, len_1 = T + w_m − t_birth (admissible iff len_1 > floor_len strictly AND t_birth > −w_m, i.e. slack_pre > 0; §1 admissibility governs).
Δ = +κ + ψ + LEDGER χ if at a return site. Admissible under caps; cap-saturated ⇒ INADMISSIBLE this round, re-eligible next (logged).

operations.case_description: FISSION(f,k,gap): episode k is split into two children by removing an interior gap (g0,g1] contained in the episode plateau.
preconditions: K_f < 4
floors fit in Ω_free
gap ⊆ plateau with margins
§1 admissibility: Ω_free > 0 must hold for the child, i.e. Ω − (K_f+1)·floor_len − K_f·floor_gap > 0 (derived instantiation of the §1 rule)

precondition_gaps.note: The numeric "margins" in "gap ⊆ plateau with margins" are not given in §1/§5; the plateau itself is [b_k+w, d_k−w] per §1.

latch_effect.rule: Interior op: latches are never touched.
latch_effect.rule_quote: interior ops (interior fission/truncation/reactivation/prune) never touch latches

endpoint_note.text: Because the split gap lies inside the plateau of episode k, both outer endpoints b_1 and d_{K_f} are preserved, consistent with "an op that preserves an outer endpoint preserves its latch".

boolean_form.formula: ℓ_pre′ = ℓ_pre(parent A) OR ℓ_pre(parent B); ℓ_post′ = ℓ_post(parent A) OR ℓ_post(parent B)
boolean_form.reasoning: A pre-latched parent has b_1 = −w_m exactly, the minimum of the admissible range, so it necessarily owns the globally earliest b_1 and its ℓ_pre is the bit inherited; if neither parent is pre-latched the inherited bit is 0 either way. Both parents cannot be pre-latched at once — they would share the endpoint −w_m, contradicting the "episode unions disjoint with floors" precondition. Symmetrically for ℓ_post at T + w_m. The OR form is therefore equivalent to the spec's owner-of-the-extreme-endpoint rule.
